newTopics.title: Fashion Design: From Idea to Garment
newTopics.summary: Fashion designers start with a figure, a mood and a few sketches, then think about fabric, shape and how clothes move on a body.
newTopics.tryIt: Pick one word — 'ocean', 'forest' or 'city'. Sketch three outfits that all share that idea through color, shape or pattern.

resources.title: Evening dress
resources.creator: House of Worth, 1895–96
resources.note: Notice the huge sleeves and narrow waist — the silhouette is the design.

resources.title: Costume in The Metropolitan Museum of Art
resources.creator: The Costume Institute
resources.note: How a museum collects and studies clothing as art.

resources.title: Costume Institute Fashion Plates (digital collection)
resources.publisher: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Watson Library
resources.note: Hundreds of historic fashion illustrations to browse for ideas.

newTopics.title: Poster Design: Bold Shapes, Few Colors
newTopics.summary: A good poster is read in a second. Artists like Toulouse-Lautrec used flat shapes, strong outlines and only a few colors to catch the eye from across the street.
keyConcepts: Lettering as part of the picture
newTopics.tryIt: Design a poster for an imaginary event using only three colors. Step back three meters — can you still read it?

resources.title: Divan Japonais
resources.creator: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, 1892–93 (color lithograph)
resources.note: Big black shapes, cropped figures and hand-drawn lettering — a model of poster design.

resources.title: How to make decorative letters | Drop-in Drawing
resources.note: Design your own letters, the way poster artists did.

newTopics.title: Pattern & Ornament: Designing with Repeats
newTopics.summary: Patterns are built from a small motif repeated in a rhythm. Designers like William Morris turned birds, leaves and flowers into fabrics and wallpapers.
newTopics.tryIt: Draw one small leaf or flower in a square. Trace it into a 3×3 grid, flipping every other square. What new shapes appear where they meet?

resources.title: Bird (woven textile)
resources.creator: William Morris, designed 1878
resources.note: Find the single bird motif, then see how it repeats across the cloth.

resources.title: How to draw a decorative border | Drop-in Drawing
Arts and Crafts movement (Art Term)
resources.note: Why designers like Morris chose handmade work and nature-inspired patterns.

newTopics.title: Drawing Spaces: Architecture and the City
newTopics.summary: Architects and painters use perspective to imagine buildings and streets before they exist. Looking at how they arrange space helps your own scenes feel real.
keyConcepts: Framing a view through an arch or window
newTopics.tryIt: Draw the view through a doorway or window at home. Use the frame of the opening as the edge of your picture.

resources.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
resources.creator: Gustave Caillebotte, 1877
resources.note: Follow the building edges — they lead your eye deep into the city.

resources.title: Design for a Painted Wall Decoration: Architectural Perspective Seen Through an Arch
resources.creator: Anonymous Italian artist, 18th century (pen, ink and watercolor)
resources.note: A painted illusion: flat wall, but it looks like you could walk through it.
